reason: Hypothesis A directly addresses the Cr–Zr interdiffusion limitation with a physically sound mechanism (alumina barrier formation) that is specific, testable, and well-grounded in oxidation science, while Hypothesis B introduces a nickel-based layer that risks low-melting eutectics with Zr at accident temperatures (~1200–1600°C) and cites irrelevant evidence (refractory HEA and steel substrate studies) that do not support its feasibility in this nuclear cladding system.
